messages:
elena: Partner reported doubled usage in APAC for 2026-09-02 02:00-03:00 window. Finance saw +100% tokens for 4 customers. Anyone seen this pattern before? :eyes:

sam: Noticed similar spikes last quarter due to partner retry semantics. Do we still dedupe solely on `usage_id`?

elena: Yes. Partner's retry flow issues new usage_id each attempt and their confirm webhook can arrive late per-region. Late confirms trigger our backfill and we re-ingest with new ids.

rahul: We need a practical idempotency strategy. Suggest composite key: `customer|meter|window_start|round(quantity,2)|region`. That should collapse retries but allow small measurement variance.

sam: Agree. Also propose storing a lightweight tombstone record when we prune an original event so billing/audit can trace credits. Tombstone = composite_key + original_usage_id + credit_ref (if any). TTL 90d?

elena: Sounds good. Can we keep tombstone searchable by invoice_id so finance workflows are easy?

rahul: Yes — include invoice_id when available and index tombstones in our billing datastore. Implementation plan: (1) ingest-time composite key check against Redis (TTL 30d), (2) backfill job to reconcile last 30 days producing tombstones for dropped rows, (3) feature-flag rollout per partner.

marketplace-bot: webhook_retry: {"url":"https://hooks.redwood.example/partner-usage","status":502,"attempts":4,"last":"2026-09-02T03:12:07Z"}

sam: Action items: rahul -> prototype key gen + unit tests (48h), elena -> collect 3 anonymized payloads and open partner ticket, finance -> confirm tombstone acceptance. I'll scope backfill cost once we know row counts.

elena: I'll schedule a short sync with partner for tomorrow and share the patch notes. Keeping thread open. :thumbsup:
